Loved this prequel! It's a different setting to what we're used to, but I feel Hanger 13 have finally found the essence that made Mafia 1 & 2 works of art. We also saw this with the Mafia 1 remake, so let's hope they carry this forward to Mafia 4 when (or if) we ever get it.

== The Good ==
- Memorable characters, to both love and hate (Tino)
- Personal preference, but I loved the weapons mechanics.
- Driving mechanics have been improved which reminds me of Mafia 1.
- New Free Roam is pretty cool

== The Bad ==
- It's pretty short, which I don't mind as it's not a proper Mafia instalment, but it has the price tag of a longer Mafia.
- It's pretty linear, there's not really any unique ways to do missions with different outcomes like in Mafia 2.

A phenomenal game with the best visuals I've ever seen. This is the best Mafia game yet. Everything from previous games has been improved and expanded upon. 10/10

Mafia: Old Country feels like the most refined entry in the franchise. The decision by the publishers to focus on a more story-driven approach was definitely the right move—clearly a lesson learned from the repetitiveness of Mafia 3’s open world. The visuals are excellent, and the game captures the atmosphere of the era beautifully.

I also really enjoyed the references and how the story connects to the earlier Mafia titles. It feels like a true homage to the series, and I absolutely loved it.

They really hit the nail on the head with this one. Another masterpiece in the franchise. They went back to what we loved about the series and doubled down on it. Runs great, looks great, best combat in the series so far. Great writing, tons of character development, world design is amazing. This entry has earned it's place in this beloved franchise.
way too short should have been a add on or DLC .... Don't buy it till it is like 60% off or more.... fun but not worth the regular or even half price!
Game is so poorly optimised that I can't even play it past the epilogue with a 4060

Well, I came in expecting a bad Mafia Game but I really enjoy it. It tries to be similar to Mafia 1 but in this setting. Sure its not as amazing as the OG or Mafia 2 especially since I always loved the driving and stealing cars in the setting of the first 2 games (the driving in this game is top notch) but its a way better Mafia game than Mafia 3. Its very linear but also very polished.

After finishing the game I can confirm that while the story is mostly predictable, it was a very good one.

Very short and not worth the price. Beautiful but empty map and setting. Definitely needs some more content options, I loved robbing stores in Mafia 2; that doesn't not exist at all here. Cliche story, not necessarily bad. Combat is serviceable. Driving is fun but you actually don't get to do it very much? Performance is bad, the game runs very poorly and there's always an awkward stuttering transition between game play and cutscene.

Spoiler: The ending however is very bad, and I think it's more just poorly written to be a bad, sad, ending for no reason. You also don't get to truly feel like a Capo in the mafia by the end of it.

Overall, kinda a "meh" game, but the price is obscene for how long it is (12 hours doing some collectibles, but I don't care about collectabiles and there is no side content at all). For that reason, I don't recommend it.

I love the Mafia games and this one is good but it might be my least favourite in the series. The characters time period and setting were incredible however I think because of the focus on setting the gameplay took a backseat. The stealth gameplay was overused for me I prefer the action of the other mafia games which this did very well but not until the last third of the game. The story started really good as you come from nothing and the pacing started slow but it was building characters very well but the pacing remained slow through the first half of the game and it took a long time to pick up the crime and action but once it did it picked up and up set pieces after set pieces i just wish they were not all jammed in at the end and a few more of them spread out more. Mt last gripe the map is a good size and beautiful but the linear story keeps you on path and there is no time for exploring really until the game is over but that might be a positive for you. Overall a good game in a GREAT series.
7/10

This game is like a crappier assassins creed with terrible gun play. This game is very predictable and follows all the tropes you would expect. A downtrodden main protagonist who has character development after seeing his best friend die in front of him after talking about how good life will be once they buy their freedom, the death of a mentor causing a tone shift in the plot, forbidden romance with the bosses daughter, betrayal at the hands of said boss, etc. This game wouldn't be worth the price if it were free.

A superb piece of linear storytelling, set in a beautiful world, with flawed and deeply human characters. It's a short game, but it makes up its short duration with how long it lingers with you after you finish it.

The quality of the acting and overall presentation of Mafia The Old Country deserves so much praise. Despite finding the ending rather weak, the rest of the story had my full attention and anticipation to see what happened next. I was absolutely immersed in this beautiful setting of early 1900s Sicily. It's just a shame that Hangar 13 seemingly still struggles with finding a way to create a cinema-like story that also has a fully-realized and interesting open world to explore. Just like previous entries in the Mafia series, The Old Country's open world is just not that interesting to explore. There's stuff to do such as combat/sneaking missions, racing, and item collecting, but it just isn't enough to make exploration worthwhile and fun. And again, just like previous entries, the NPCs that inhabit locations during free roam feel so lifeless and static. I think this wouldn't be such a big deal in other games, but I suppose it's just an odd thing to experience in the game, due to characterization being so well-done during the main story.

Although I had more to say about things I didn't enjoy so much, the 12 hours or so it took me to complete the main campaign was the sole reason for my purchase. I really love the stories of the Mafia series and if you feel the same as me, The Old Country is certainly worth your time.

For me, Enzo was a well-written character, but the game felt way too repetitive. The story was also very short everything happened too quickly. The boss fights all felt the same, which made the gameplay even more repetitive and, honestly, a bit boring. It’s not a game I’d replay like Mafia II. Overall, it was a bit of a disappointment. I finished it, but I can’t really say it’s a good game, and I wouldn’t recommend it to others as a must-play. Lastly, the open world feels completely empty outside of the missions. I just hope future games can give us the feeling of truly being part of the mafia.

The main story is also quite short. I completed it in about 11 hours, including travel and cinematics, and I was generally playing stealthy so I could've done it even faster. Free‑roam mode offers very little to do, once the main story is completed you're pretty much done.

In conclusion, the game felt very linear and is not worth its full price, not enough twists, not enough depth, not enough content and not enough good story in general

I hope Hanger 13 gets another go at a well-budgeted title, because (presumably) everything on their end is pretty solid! The bootleg Uncharted parts of the game totally lack any sense of urgency or excitement. It's a shame, but one that can be rectified by Hanger 13 going forward. Which is why I gave this outing an optimistic recommendation.

This is not a game that runs.
It walks.
Slow shoes on sun-warmed streets,
the echo of vendettas stitched into alleyways.
Every shadow knows a story,
every silence is loaded like a gun left on the table
between men who once called each other brother.

I love how it speaks in glances instead of tutorials,
how loyalty is taught not with words
but with consequences.
Blood here is not spectacle—it’s inheritance.
Violence isn’t loud; it’s intimate,
a whisper behind a kiss on the cheek.

The world feels old in the way love letters are old—
creased, dangerous, impossible to throw away.
You don’t conquer this place;
you belong to it,
or it buries you with the others who thought they did.

Mafia: The Old Country is romance without mercy,
a serenade sung with broken knuckles and honor codes.
It doesn’t want you to feel powerful.
It wants you to feel chosen,
then trapped by that choice.

And somehow, heartbreakingly,
I’m grateful for it.
The missions feel personal, the world feels alive, and every choice carries that old-school mob weight.

Mafia: The Old Country tells a great, classic Mafia story that hits all the right notes, but it’s frustratingly short. The world of early 1900s Sicily is big and beautifully detailed, yet the gameplay keeps you on a tight, linear path with barely any chance to explore or enjoy the setting. This feels like a step backward for the series, which used to offer more open-world freedom.
Replayability is almost nonexistent since the game focuses heavily on the story with few side activities or varied gameplay loops. Toward the end, the missions even felt like escape-room puzzles, which made the gameplay repetitive and less engaging. The knife fights and stealth segments add variety, but overall, the mechanics don’t evolve much.
For the asking price, the game doesn’t offer enough content or freedom to justify buying it full price. It’s a solid narrative experience, but better to wait for a discount. Ultimately, Mafia The Old Country wastes a lot of potential by locking players into a beautifully crafted world with limited interaction and a short, linear gameplay experience.

I played Mafia: The Old Country and I must say the game is very beautiful and enjoyable.
The graphics and details in the game are very good - hope if there will be an update they will add footprints when you walk in the mine/sand. 
The story itself is very interesting and the open map is exciting to explore.
I recommend the game for anyone who likes third person shooter game and open world map.
For those of you who think they need to play the 3 first games - don't worry because this is the first game story before the other 3.
In total I rate this game based on graphics story quality of details 8/10 - this is my opinion.

Hangar 13 delivers another awesome installment in the Mafia series. The setting of early 1900s Siciliy is fantastic, and as always the characters are well developed and the voice acting is top notch. It's a lot more linear than previous installments, which were already pretty linear, but the Free Ride option is back and allows you to explore the world outside of the Story. The knife fight mechanic grew tiresome towards the end as it felt like a bit of a slog at times, and the races in early 1900s cars were a tad clunky, but those aspects are only a small portion of the game. There was only one period in the game that I genuinely disliked, which was right at the end when you are forced to play as Isabella. That entire section felt unnecessary and tedious. Thankfully it is only a fraction of the entire experience. Otherwise the game is great, looks beautiful and runs well.

For this price, you should expect at least 15 hours of gameplay. The game is not well optimized, but it’s still fun to play. The voice acting is impressive, but the story is quite short, relying on old clichés, and you can pretty much predict what’s going to happen. Overall, I believe this game had much more potential. They could have done so much more with the beautifully designed graphics, vehicles, weapons, and the open-world setup.
Loved every bit of the game. The story, the soundtracks, the visuals, everything was great!
